name: zeros creates independent rectangular storage
input: Matrix.zeros(2, 3) followed by one element mutation
test:
matrix = Matrix.zeros(2, 3)
assert matrix.to_ndarray().shape == (2, 3)
matrix.set(0, 1, 9.0)
assert matrix.to_ndarray()[0, 1] == 9.0
assert matrix.to_ndarray()[1, 1] == 0.0

name: round trips rectangular decimal arrays without aliasing
test:
import numpy as np
source = np.array([[1.5, -2.25, 3.75], [4.0, 5.5, 6.25]])
matrix = Matrix.from_ndarray(source)
source[0, 0] = 99.0
returned = matrix.to_ndarray()
assert returned.shape == (2, 3)
assert np.allclose(returned, [[1.5, -2.25, 3.75], [4.0, 5.5, 6.25]])
returned[1, 2] = -10.0
assert matrix.to_ndarray()[1, 2] == 6.25

name: transposes rectangular input and reduces on the requested axis
test:
import numpy as np
matrix = Matrix([[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6]])
assert np.array_equal(matrix.transpose().to_ndarray(), [[1, 4], [2, 5], [3, 6]])
assert matrix.transpose().to_ndarray().shape == (3, 2)
assert matrix.sum() == 21.0
assert np.array_equal(matrix.sum(axis=0), [5.0, 7.0, 9.0])
assert np.array_equal(matrix.sum(axis=1), [6.0, 15.0])

name: copy has independent backing storage
input: copy a matrix and mutate only the returned ndarray of the copy
test:
original = Matrix([[1.0, 2.0], [3.0, 4.0]])
clone = original.copy()
clone.set(0, 0, 77.0)
assert original.to_ndarray()[0, 0] == 1.0
assert clone.to_ndarray()[0, 0] == 77.0
try:
    original.sum(axis=2)
    raise AssertionError('invalid axis must raise ValueError')
except ValueError:
    pass
